name: Seoul · Jeju · Busan
tagline: Seoul's palaces, then a volcanic island of silver-grass craters, sea cliffs and divers' seafood, finishing on Busan's coast.
summary: Three full Seoul days, then three on Jeju with a car: oreum craters covered in silver grass, Hallasan's alpine plateau, Olle-trail sea cliffs, Sunrise Peak and Udo. Busan gets a day and a half for its seaside temple, the sky capsule, the fish market and the drone show. It suits travelers who want open landscape and coast more than temples and tombs, and are happy to drive.
design_notes: Seoul days 17-19 are the classic option's (Gyeongbokgung on Monday because it closes on Tuesday).
Jeju is one base on the south coast for three nights instead of hopping around the island; the east day (Seongsan, Udo) is the long drive.
Tue 20 flies from Gimpo (Line 5 from Jongno, no transfer). Jeju → Busan on Fri 23 avoids backtracking to Seoul.
Seongsan sunrise is optional (05:20 departure); the default plan climbs at 08:00 and reaches Udo before the tour groups.
Busan Fri-Sat uses Gwangalli-Planet16 (2-night minimum, live-checked), which fits this route exactly. The omakase is Friday lunch at Iwa on the way in from the airport.
Jeju hotels were not live-checked; prices are estimates. Check them first, because the National Sports Festival fills the island Oct 16-22.

japan_matches.korea: Busan's east coast on Friday: Haedong Yonggungsa on its sea rocks, Cheongsapo's lighthouses and the Sky Capsule on the old shore railway. Jeju adds Olle trail 7's sea cliffs and Seogwipo's small-town harbor.
japan_matches.honest_note: Jeju is volcanic and rural, with no old temple town; the temple-by-the-sea moment comes in Busan.

japan_matches.korea: Saturday night in Mangwon and Hongdae, Monday in Euljiro's back-alley bars, Gwangjang Market, and the Gwangalli drone show on Saturday in Busan.
japan_matches.honest_note: There's no scramble crossing; Myeongdong and Gangnam have the bigger-neon look if you want it.

japan_matches.korea: Sanbangsan's carbonated hot spring under the lava dome (Tue 20) and Hurshimchung in Busan (Sat 24). Splurge tier: the Pinx Podo Hotel, with hot-spring water in every room.
japan_matches.honest_note: Below the splurge tier there's no ryokan-style night on this route; the soaks are public bathhouses.

japan_matches.korea: Iwa's aged-fish omakase lunch in Haeundae, plus haenyeo-caught abalone on Jeju and Jagalchi's pick-your-fish raw fish.
japan_matches.honest_note: Iwa is Japanese-style sushi by Korean chefs; the Jeju seafood is homestyle, not a counter.

highlights: Three Seoul days: Secret Garden, Gyeongbokgung in hanbok, Haneul Park's silver grass
Saebyeol Oreum's silver-grass ridge at sunset after a carbonated hot-spring soak
Hallasan's Yeongsil trail to the alpine plateau, then Olle trail 7's sea cliffs
Seongsan Ilchulbong and a morning by e-bike on Udo
Iwa's omakase lunch, Haedong Yonggungsa and the Sky Capsule in Busan
Jagalchi, Gamcheon, Hurshimchung and the Saturday drone show
tradeoffs: No peak foliage: Hallasan peaks in early November. Silver grass on the oreum is the autumn show.
Jeju's National Sports Festival (Oct 16-22) overlaps your Jeju nights: hotels and cars are tight and pricier, and the Jeju prices here are estimates.

Driving: a rental car needs a physical International Driving Permit from AAA before you fly (same day at an AAA office, about US$20). Without one, 8-hour taxi tours cost about ₩180,000 per car per day.
Two domestic flights and more weather risk: Udo ferries, Yongmeori and Hallasan trails close in wind or rain.
No Gyeongju: history is the Seoul palaces and the National Museum.

days.title: Dawn landing, hanok lanes, silver-grass sunset
days.summary: Taxi straight to a room that is already yours (booked from Oct 16), sleep until lunch, then an easy hanok-lane stroll and the opening evening of the Seoul Eulalia Festival. Hongdae's Saturday-night buzz is there if anyone still has energy.
days.autumn_note: Opening day of the 25th Seoul Eulalia (silver grass) Festival at Haneul Park, 10:00-21:00 with evening lighting; the plumes are at peak. Sunset ~17:55.

items.title: Land at Incheon T1, immigration and bags
items.detail: File the free e-Arrival Card online in the 3 days before (US citizens are K-ETA-exempt through 2026). Buy a T-money or WOWPASS card at a convenience store for subways later.

items.title: Taxi to the Jongno hotel
items.detail: Regular taxi from the rank, ~70-80k KRW per car with tolls. Dawn traffic is light, about an hour door to door.

items.title: Check in (Oct 16 night booked) and sleep
items.detail: Because the room is booked from the night of Oct 16 it is ready on arrival: shower, breakfast (included at 4rest Stay), then a proper nap. This is what makes the rest of the day work.

items.title: Ikseon-dong hanok alleys + lunch
items.detail: A tight warren of 1920s urban hanok turned into cafes and dumpling shops, 5 minutes from the hotel. Small-scale, Kamakura-Komachi-dori energy.
items.tip: Weekend lunchtime queues are real; if Changhwadang has a line, any cafe courtyard works.

items.title: Bukchon lanes and Samcheong-dong
items.detail: Walk up through Gahoe-dong's tiled-roof lanes for the view toward Namsan, then down Samcheong-dong's cafe street. Keep voices low: people live here.
items.tip: The red zone (Bukchon-ro 11-gil) is open to visitors only 10:00-17:00, with fines up to 100,000 KRW outside those hours.

items.title: Haneul Park silver-grass festival at sunset
items.detail: Taxi ~30 min (~20k per car) to World Cup Park, ride the Maengkkongi cart or climb the 291 Haneul stairs, and walk the hilltop sea of silver plumes as the sun drops over the Han River. Stay for the evening lighting after ~18:15.
items.cost_note: cart one way (unconfirmed 2026 fare); free on foot
items.tip: Saturday afternoon is the busiest slot of the festival week; the crowd thins after dark.

items.title: Mangwon Market dinner, optional Hongdae
items.detail: 10 min by taxi down the hill: graze Mangwon Market's fried chicken, kalguksu and hotteok stalls. If jet lag allows, it is 10 more minutes to Hongdae's Saturday-night busking on Eoulmadang-ro, the closest thing to Shibuya crossing energy. Taxi back to Jongno ~25 min.

food.name: Changhwadang (Ikseon-dong)
food.note: Hand-made dumplings and tteokbokki in a hanok; the easy first Korean meal. Walk-in.

food.name: Mangwon Market stalls
food.note: Dakgangjeong (crispy glazed chicken), kalguksu and croquettes; stalls run to about 21:00, some close earlier.

days.rainy_swap: Swap Haneul Park for the National Museum of Korea (free, open to 21:00 on Saturdays, 'Our Dining Table' special exhibition to Oct 25), then dinner in Ikseon-dong.

days.title: Secret Garden by day, palace pond by night
days.summary: The royal Secret Garden tour in the morning, Insadong and Jogyesa at an easy pace, an afternoon rest, then Gwangjang Market and the lantern-lit pond show at Changgyeonggung. Sunday is the right day: Changdeokgung and Changgyeonggung are closed Monday.
days.autumn_note: Huwon's maples are just starting (peak is late Oct-early Nov); Changgyeonggung's Chundangji pond is one of the better palace foliage spots.

items.title: Changdeokgung + Huwon (Secret Garden) tour
items.detail: Walk the UNESCO palace (Injeongjeon, Nakseonjae), then the ~90-min guided tour through the wooded rear garden to Buyongji pond and the Ongnyucheon stream, the closest Seoul gets to a Kamakura temple garden.
items.booking: Huwon tickets release online 6 days ahead at 10:00 KST: for Oct 18 that is Mon Oct 12 10:00 KST = Sun Oct 11 21:00 in Newark. Pick an English or Korean slot around 10:30-11:30. Limited on-site tickets exist but sell out on autumn Sundays.
items.tip: The palace is 10 min on foot from 4rest Stay.

items.title: Insadong + Jogyesa temple
items.detail: Lunch on Insadong-gil, browse the craft shops and Ssamziegil, then step into Jogyesa, the working head temple of Korean Zen under 500-year-old trees.
items.tip: Jogyesa's chrysanthemum display usually starts mid-late October.

items.title: Hotel break
items.detail: Day 2 of jet lag: nap now so the evening works.

items.title: Gwangjang Market food alley
items.detail: The 1905 covered market: mung-bean bindaetteok fried to order, beef yukhoe, mayak gimbap and makgeolli at the counters. Food stalls are open on Sundays even though fabric shops close.
items.tip: Prices are posted since the 2023-24 overcharging scandals; check before ordering.

items.title: Changgyeonggung 'Mulbit Yeonhwa' night show
items.detail: Short taxi north. The palace stays open to 21:00; the media-art pond show runs at 19:00, 19:30 and 20:00 (~16 min) and the 1909 glass botanical house is lit.
items.booking: Ticketlink or Creatrip (foreigners), 1,000 KRW including admission; book a 19:30 slot now.

items.title: Jongno 3-ga tent bars (optional)
items.detail: Orange-tarp pojangmacha tents on the sidewalk: soju, grilled fish, gizzards. A yatai/yokocho night 10 min from bed.

food.name: Gaeseong Mandu Koong (Insadong)
food.note: Long-running Insadong house for North Korean-style dumplings and mandu-guk. Walk-in; confirm it is open on the day.

food.name: Gwangjang Market crawl: Soonhee-ne bindaetteok + Buchon Yukhoe
food.note: Share a bindaetteok, a yukhoe plate and a bottle of makgeolli; Buchon Yukhoe queues on Sunday evenings.

food.name: Jongno 3-ga pojangmacha
food.note: Some tents take Sunday off; pick a busy one.

days.rainy_swap: Huwon tours run in light rain (bring umbrellas). If it pours, skip the garden for Leeum Museum (open Sunday, closed Monday) or the National Museum of Korea; Mulbit is weather-dependent, so swap it for SPAREX Dongdaemun jjimjilbang.

days.title: Hanbok at the main palace, sunset on the city wall
days.summary: Monday is Gyeongbokgung's day (it closes Tuesday): wear hanbok for free entry and the guard ceremony, lunch in Seochon, then the short, steep Inwangsan fortress-wall hike for sunset over the palace and Bugaksan. Finish in Euljiro's retro back-alley bars.
days.autumn_note: Clear October air makes the Inwangsan view sharp; ginkgos around Gyeongbokgung are starting to yellow. Sunset ~17:53.

items.title: Hanbok rental near Gyeongbokgung
items.detail: Pick a shop by Gyeongbokgung station (exit 4/5) or Anguk. Basic 4-hour rental; hair styling extra.
items.booking: Walk-in, or book on Creatrip/Klook for a small discount.
items.tip: Return times are strict; ask for warm inner layers.

items.title: Gyeongbokgung Palace in hanbok
items.detail: Free in hanbok. See the 10:00 royal guard change at Gwanghwamun, Gyeonghoeru pavilion on its pond and Hyangwonjeong at the back. Geunjeongjeon's courtyard is partly fenced for works until Oct 31, but the throne hall is still visible.

items.title: Return hanbok, lunch in Seochon
items.detail: Tosokchon's ginseng chicken soup is a 5-minute walk west of the palace.

items.title: Seochon lanes, galleries and a cafe break
items.detail: Wander the hanok alleys west of the palace (Nuha-dong, Ogin-dong), small galleries and bookshops; rest over coffee before the climb.
items.tip: Many Tongin Market stalls and the dosirak cafe close on Mondays; don't plan lunch around them.

items.title: Inwangsan fortress-wall sunset hike
items.detail: From Sajik Park follow the 600-year-old city wall up the granite ridge to the 338 m summit (about 50-60 min, many stairs). Watch the sun go down behind you as Gyeongbokgung, Bugaksan and Namsan light up; descend the lit stairs.
items.tip: Bring a headlamp/phone light and water; sneakers with grip.

items.title: BBQ dinner, then Euljiro 'Hipjiro' bars
items.detail: Taxi to Geumdwaeji for charcoal-grilled pork, then 3 subway stops to Euljiro 3-ga: Nogari Alley's plastic tables, draft beer and hidden 3rd-floor bars among the print shops. Monday is a good night here (some places shut Sunday).

food.name: Tosokchon Samgyetang
food.note: Whole young chicken stuffed with sticky rice and ginseng. Fast-moving queue. Splurge alternative: Onjium (Joseon court cuisine above the palace wall, ~200k, CatchTable, hard to get).

food.name: Geumdwaeji Sikdang
food.note: Cult samgyeopsal and bone-in pork over briquettes, Seoul's Korean-BBQ benchmark. Daily 11:30-23:00; walk-in queue, so register and wait.

food.name: Euljiro Nogari Alley
food.note: Draft beer ~5,000 and dried pollock sticks ~2,500.

days.rainy_swap: Gyeongbokgung works under umbrellas (skip the hanbok). Replace Inwangsan with the National Museum of Korea (open Mondays, free), then Euljiro as planned.

days.title: Fly to the volcano island: sea cliffs, a carbonated soak, silver grass at sunset
days.summary: A one-hour flight from Gimpo, a rental car, and west Jeju: the layered sea cliffs at Yongmeori under Sanbangsan's lava dome, a soak in Sanbangsan's carbonated hot spring, then up Saebyeol Oreum, a volcanic cone covered in silver grass, for sunset.
days.autumn_note: Silver grass (eoksae) on Jeju's oreum is at its prime mid-October to early November. Tangerines are still greenish. Sunset about 17:56.

items.title: Subway to Gimpo Airport
items.detail: Line 5 from Jongno 3-ga runs straight to Gimpo Airport, about 45 minutes with no transfer (₩1,550). Taxi with bags: about ₩35,000 for the car.

items.title: Flight Gimpo → Jeju
items.detail: About 110 flights a day. Domestic check-in closes 30-40 min before departure; passport as ID.
items.booking: Korean Air, Asiana, Jeju Air or Jin Air sites; book now (Sports Festival week)

items.title: Pick up the rental car
items.detail: Shuttle from the airport to the rental-car house. Bring your passport, US license and the physical AAA International Driving Permit. Take full-coverage insurance.
items.cost_note: 3 days incl. insurance and fuel, split 3 ways (estimate)

items.title: Gogi-guksu lunch in Jeju City
items.detail: Jeju's pork-broth noodle soup with thick slices of pork, 10 minutes from the airport.

items.title: Drive to Sanbangsan
items.detail: About an hour southwest across the island.

items.title: Yongmeori coast and Sanbangsan
items.detail: A walk at the foot of sandstone cliffs layered like a dragon's head, below the bell-shaped lava dome of Sanbangsan. Yongmeori opens only when tide and waves allow (last entry 16:30); check the sign at the gate.

items.title: Sanbangsan Carbonated Hot Spring
items.detail: Cool carbonated spring water indoors and warm outdoor pools facing Sanbangsan. Swimsuits for the outdoor section.

items.title: Saebyeol Oreum silver grass at sunset
items.detail: A steep 20-30 minute climb up a grass-covered volcanic cone; at the top the silver grass glows against the sunset over the western sea. Windy: bring a layer.

items.title: Drive to Seogwipo
items.detail: About 40 minutes to the hotel area.

items.title: Galchi dinner at Negeori Sikdang
items.detail: Hairtail braised in spicy sauce or grilled whole: Seogwipo's signature.

food.name: Jamae Guksu
food.note: Gogi-guksu with a rich pork broth; a local favorite near the airport.

food.name: Negeori Sikdang
food.note: Galchi jorim (braised hairtail) for the table.

days.rainy_swap: Yongmeori closes in big waves anyway. In rain, spend longer in the hot spring and swap Saebyeol for ARTE Museum Jeju (indoor media art, about ₩18,000) on the way back.

days.title: Hallasan's alpine plateau, then the south-coast cliffs and falls
days.summary: A morning hike up Hallasan's Yeongsil trail past a crown of rock pinnacles to the high plateau, then the south coast: Jusangjeolli's hexagonal basalt columns, Olle trail 7 along the cliffs to Oedolgae, and Seogwipo's market for dinner.
days.autumn_note: Hallasan's upper slopes show early color (its peak is about Nov 6-13); the plateau is golden with dwarf bamboo and grass. It is 8-10°C colder up top.

items.title: Drive to the Yeongsil trailhead
items.detail: The upper car park is small and fills early; arrive by about 08:00.

items.title: Hallasan Yeongsil trail to Witse-oreum
items.detail: The most scenic route on Hallasan: steep stairs past the Yeongsil Giam pinnacles and the Byeongpungbawi cliff, then a flat boardwalk across the alpine plateau to the Witse-oreum shelter. About 3.7 km each way. No booking needed (summit routes need one; this isn't a summit route).
items.tip: Not hikers? Spend the morning at Camellia Hill or the O'sulloc tea fields instead.

items.title: Lunch in Jungmun
items.detail: Abalone porridge or seafood ramyeon near the resort area.

items.title: Jusangjeolli cliffs
items.detail: Hexagonal basalt columns where lava met the sea, with waves crashing up the pillars.

items.title: Olle trail 7: Oedolgae cliffs
items.detail: The most loved section of Jeju's coastal trail: pine-topped cliffs, a 20 m sea stack (Oedolgae) and views to the offshore islets.

items.title: Saeyeon Bridge and Cheonjiyeon Falls
items.detail: The sail-shaped footbridge to Saeseom islet at sunset, then the waterfall in its lit gorge after dark.

items.title: Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market
items.detail: Graze: sashimi platters, black-pork skewers, tangerine juice, and hotteok.

food.name: Abalone porridge in Jungmun
food.note: Green-tinted porridge cooked with abalone innards; a Jeju staple.

food.name: Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market grazing
food.note: Buy a takeaway sashimi box and black-pork skewers; eat in the market's seating areas.

days.rainy_swap: Hallasan trails close in heavy rain or strong wind. Swap the hike for the Jeju Stone Park or ARTE Museum, and keep the coast for the afternoon if it clears.

days.title: Sunrise Peak, a morning on Udo, and a rolling crater at dusk
days.summary: Climb Seongsan Ilchulbong, the tuff-cone crater rising from the sea, then a 15-minute ferry to Udo for a loop by e-bike past white-sand beaches. Abalone lunch on the east coast, the ancient nutmeg forest at Bijarim, and Yongnuni Oreum's soft green-gold ridges for sunset.
days.autumn_note: Yongnuni's silver grass and the low autumn light make the crater ridges glow. Sunrise about 06:39 (optional), sunset about 17:54.

items.title: Drive east to Seongsan
items.detail: About an hour from Seogwipo. For sunrise on the summit, leave at 05:20 instead.

items.title: Seongsan Ilchulbong (Sunrise Peak)
items.detail: A 20-30 minute stair climb up a 5,000-year-old tuff cone to the rim of a crater 600 m across, with the sea on three sides.
items.tip: The haenyeo (women divers) have historically performed at the beach below the peak's west side at 13:30 and 15:00; check on the day.

items.title: Udo island
items.detail: Ferry from Seongsan port (15 min, every 30 min; the car stays behind). Rent e-bikes to loop the island: Hagosu-dong beach, Seobin white sand made of red algae, and peanut ice cream.

items.title: Abalone lunch on the east coast
items.detail: Abalone hot-pot rice at Myeongjin Jeonbok, run by a haenyeo family.

items.title: Bijarim forest
items.detail: Thousands of 500-800-year-old nutmeg yews on a soft red-volcanic-scoria path.

items.title: Yongnuni Oreum at sunset
items.detail: A gentle 30-minute climb to a triple crater rim of grass and silver grass, with Seongsan and the sea on the horizon.

items.title: Drive back to Seogwipo
items.detail: About 50 minutes.

items.title: Jeju black pork BBQ
items.detail: Thick-cut heukdwaeji grilled over charcoal, dipped in anchovy sauce.

food.name: Myeongjin Jeonbok
food.note: Jeonbok dolsotbap (abalone stone-pot rice); queue or use the waitlist tablet.

food.name: Jeju black pork BBQ (Seogwipo)
food.note: Order ogyeopsal (skin-on belly) and moksal (neck).

days.rainy_swap: Udo ferries stop in strong wind. Instead: the Haenyeo Museum (open Thursdays), Bijarim, and Seongsan if the rain allows, then an early dinner.

days.title: Over the mountain to the airport, an omakase lunch, the Busan coast
days.summary: A last drive across Hallasan's forested flank, an hour's flight to Busan, then the best of its east coast on a weekday: an omakase lunch in Haeundae, Haedong Yonggungsa on its sea rocks, and the pastel Sky Capsule along the old shore railway at golden hour.
days.autumn_note: Today is 상강 (Sanggang), 'frost descent', the last solar term of autumn. Busan stays green; the draw is the clear sea air. Sunset about 17:46.

items.title: Drive the 5.16 road to the airport
items.detail: Route 1131 climbs through Hallasan's forest past the Saryeoni cedar woods; stop for 20 minutes if there's time. Refuel before returning the car.

items.title: Return the rental car
items.detail: Shuttle back to the terminal.

items.title: Flight Jeju → Busan
items.detail: Many daily flights (Korean Air, Jin Air, Jeju Air, Air Busan).

items.title: Taxi to Gwangalli-Planet16, drop bags
items.detail: About ₩30,000 for the car.

items.title: Omakase lunch at Iwa, Haeundae
items.detail: Aged-fish sushi omakase at a Michelin-selected counter: the trip's sushi moment.
items.booking: Phone +82 10-8543-3356; ask your hotel to call. Book now.

items.title: Haedong Yonggungsa seaside temple
items.detail: A temple built onto the sea rocks, reached down 108 steps, with waves breaking under the halls.

items.title: Cheongsapo twin lighthouses
items.detail: The red and white lighthouses on the breakwater, and the clear-floored Daritdol Skywalk.

items.title: Sky Capsule Cheongsapo → Mipo
items.detail: Your own pastel pod creeps along the old coastal railway above the shore for 30 minutes into Haeundae.
items.booking: Blueline Park site or Klook; weekdays are easier

items.title: Haeundae Beach at sunset
items.detail: Walk the length of the beach toward Dongbaek Island.

items.title: Light dinner in Haeundae
items.detail: Pufferfish soup at Geumsu Bokguk after the big lunch.

food.name: Iwa (sushi omakase)
food.note: Aged-fish nigiri, lunch course; confirm the closed day when booking.

food.name: Geumsu Bokguk (Haeundae flagship)
food.note: Clear pufferfish soup, a Busan classic since 1970.

days.rainy_swap: Flights rarely cancel in ordinary rain. In Busan the capsule runs in normal rain; in a storm swap it for Spa Land Centum and keep Haedong Yonggungsa if the sea is safe.

days.title: Painted hills, the fish market, a hot-spring soak, drones over the bridge
days.summary: Gamcheon's pastel hillside early, lunch upstairs at Jagalchi on fish you pick yourselves, an afternoon in Korea's largest hot-spring bathhouse, then raw fish facing Gwangan Bridge and the Saturday drone show from the beach outside your hotel.
days.autumn_note: Jeon-eo (gizzard shad) and galchi are the autumn picks at Jagalchi. Drone show theme Oct 24: 'Forest's Melody'.

items.title: Gamcheon Culture Village
items.detail: Taxi ~35 min (~25k per car) to the top and walk down through the pastel refugee-era houses, art installations and the Little Prince lookout before the tour groups.

items.title: Jagalchi Fish Market: pick it, eat it upstairs
items.detail: Taxi ~15 min. Choose live fish on the ground floor, have it sliced and eat on 2F with a view of the harbor; finish with a spicy maeuntang from the bones.
items.tip: Agree the price per kg and weight before the knife goes in.

items.title: BIFF Square and Gukje Market
items.detail: Seed-stuffed ssiat hotteok from the BIFF stalls, then the postwar Gukje Market alleys. Coffee break nearby.

items.title: Hurshimchung hot spring (Dongnae)
items.detail: Metro or taxi (~30 min) to Oncheonjang: about 40 baths under a glass dome fed by the 1,300-year-old Dongnae spring, including open-air and cypress tubs. Reopened May 2026 after renovation.
items.tip: Bathing is nude and gender-separated; tattoos are generally tolerated.

items.title: Millak hoe facing Gwangan Bridge
items.detail: Buy fish on 1F of the Millak fishermen's market and eat upstairs as the bridge lights come on.

items.title: Gwangalli M Drone Light Show
items.detail: About 1,100 drones over the bridge for ~12 minutes at 19:00 and again at 21:00. Watch the first from the sand in front of the hotel, then a beach bar, and catch the quieter 21:00 show.
items.tip: Arrive 30 min early for a central spot. Cancelled for wind or rain with little notice.

food.name: Jagalchi Market hoe (2F restaurants)
food.note: Platter for 3 ~60-120k plus ~5,000 pp table fee. The freshest raw fish of the trip.

food.name: BIFF Square ssiat hotteok
food.note: Fried pancake stuffed with brown sugar and seeds.

food.name: Millak Fishermen's Live Fish Market
food.note: Flatfish ~30k/kg, setting fee ~6,000 pp; ask for a window table. Go by 17:30: the drone show fills every seat.

days.rainy_swap: Jagalchi and Gukje Market are covered and Hurshimchung is indoors. If the drone show is cancelled, watch the bridge lights from a Gwangalli bar.

days.title: Slow beach morning, KTX north, fly home
days.summary: A lazy Gwangalli morning, milmyeon by Busan Station, then the KTX to Seoul and the AREX straight to the airport with time to spare.

items.title: Gwangalli beach morning
items.detail: Coffee and a beach walk; Millak Waterfront Park at the north end for one last bridge view.

items.title: Check out, taxi to Busan Station
items.detail: ~30 min (~20k per car).

items.title: Milmyeon lunch by the station
items.detail: Choryang's wartime-refugee cold wheat noodles, a 5-minute walk from Busan Station.

items.title: KTX Busan → Seoul
items.detail: KTX-Sancheon 38.
items.booking: Korail+ / korail.com, book now (Sunday northbound sells out).

items.title: AREX Express to Incheon T1
items.detail: Non-stop 43 min. At the airport ~17:00 for the 21:55 flight; eat and shop airside.

items.title: Air Premia departs ICN
items.detail: Confirm the terminal (T1 assumed) the day before.

food.name: Gwangalli beachfront cafe
food.note: Any bridge-view cafe on Gwanganhaebyeon-ro.

food.name: Choryang Milmyeon
food.note: Busan-only cold noodles; mul (broth) or bibim (spicy).

days.rainy_swap: Nothing changes; spend the morning at a cafe or Spa Land Centum (lockers for bags) before the train.

stays.why_area: Walking distance to Changdeokgung, Bukchon, Ikseon-dong, Insadong and Gwangjang Market, with subway Lines 1, 3 and 5 for everything else.

choices.name: 4rest Stay Jongno
choices.room: Deluxe Suite: 1 twin + 1 full bed (max 3), breakfast included
choices.price_basis: Live Booking.com Oct 6: 1,475,638 with tax for Oct 16-21 (5 nights) and 1,201,323 for Oct 16-19 (3 weekend nights), non-refundable. 4 nights (Fri-Mon) should land near 1.36M.
choices.why: Cheapest live room with a real bed for each of you, breakfast included, 3 minutes from Jongmyo and Ikseon-dong.

choices.name: Nine Tree by Parnas Dongdaemun
choices.room: Family Room: twin + full bed, 1 room
choices.price_basis: Live Booking.com Oct 6: 1,736,141 with tax for Oct 16-21 (5 nights), free cancellation until Oct 13, no prepayment
choices.availability: partly sold out · a later Oct 6 search found no rooms for Oct 16-19
choices.why: Free cancellation and a proper family room, two subway stops from Jongno. Recheck: it may be gone for the weekend.

notes: Lodging is for 3 people sharing one room each night, 8 core nights Oct 17-24. The Oct 16 night is shown separately.

Seoul and Busan prices are live checks from Oct 6 2026 (taxes included). Jeju prices are estimates from Oct 2026 price snapshots, not live availability: the Sports Festival (Oct 16-22) makes that week tight.
Busan has no sweet tier: Planet16 is the only live Fri-Sat room on the drone-show beach. The splurge pick (Ananti Cove) puts the splurge total well over US$1,000.
Intercity transport covers the airport taxi share, two domestic flights, the Jeju rental car with insurance and fuel (estimate), the Gimhae taxi, the Busan-Seoul KTX and the AREX.
Local transit (about 95,000 per person) covers Seoul and Busan subway rides and taxis, split 3 ways, plus Jeju parking.
Food is excluded. Typical spend is 50,000-80,000 per person per day, plus Iwa's omakase lunch (about 80,000).

watch_outs: Without a physical IDP you can't rent a car on Jeju; a photo or a digital copy isn't accepted.
Jeju weather: Udo ferries stop in strong wind, Yongmeori opens only when tide and waves allow, and Hallasan trails close in heavy rain. Have the indoor swaps ready.
Seoul closures: Mon Oct 19 Changdeokgung, Changgyeonggung and Deoksugung; the plan puts Gyeongbokgung on Monday because it closes Tuesday.
Low-cost domestic flights allow 15 kg checked; overweight fees are charged at the counter.
The Gwangalli drone show is cancelled in rain or strong wind.
Air Premia can't use Seoul Station city check-in; ride the AREX with your bags and reach T1 by about 17:00.
